plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payout item record was created.

models.name: shopping_mall_inventory_items
models.description:
Per-SKU inventory state for each sellable variant.

Represents the authoritative stock position for a single product SKU, including on-hand and reserved quantities. This model is the core reference for inventory-related decisions in cart validation, checkout, and fulfillment.

Each record is linked to exactly one SKU in {@link shopping_mall_product_skus}. It exposes normalized quantitative fields and status flags. Detailed configuration for backorders and preorders is stored in {@link shopping_mall_backorder_settings} and {@link shopping_mall_preorder_settings} via 1:1 relationships.

Soft deletion is supported via deleted_at to allow historical reconstruction without losing past inventory states. Any available-to-sell figures should be computed dynamically from on_hand_quantity and reserved_quantity or via materialized views, not stored redundantly in this table.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the inventory item record.

foreignFields.name: product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Target SKU whose inventory is being tracked. {@link shopping_mall_product_skus.id}.

plainFields.name: on_hand_quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units physically available in storage for this SKU, not yet sold or reserved.

plainFields.name: reserved_quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units currently reserved for pending orders that are not yet fully paid or fulfilled.

plainFields.name: low_stock_threshold
plainFields.description: Optional threshold at or below which this SKU should be considered low stock for alerts and catalog signals.

plainFields.name: stock_status
plainFields.description: Current stock status flag such as in_stock, low_stock, out_of_stock, backorder_allowed, or preorder_only. Business logic interprets allowed values.

plainFields.name: backorder_enabled
plainFields.description: Indicates whether backorders are allowed for this SKU based on current configuration and policies.

plainFields.name: preorder_enabled
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this SKU is currently available for preorder only, before normal stock is available.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this inventory item record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this inventory item record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this inventory item record was soft-deleted. Null when the record is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_inventory_reservations
models.description:
Temporary reservations of inventory units linked to orders and order lines.

Each reservation represents a portion of stock held for a given order line while payment and checkout are in progress. Reservations prevent overselling by reducing the available-to-sell quantity without immediately decrementing on-hand stock.

Reservations may expire when payment is not completed within configured windows. They are always linked to an {@link shopping_mall_inventory_items} record and usually to {@link shopping_mall_orders} and {@link shopping_mall_order_lines}.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the inventory reservation record.

foreignFields.name: inventory_item_id
foreignFields.description: Inventory item whose quantity is being temporarily reserved. {@link shopping_mall_inventory_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Order for which this reservation was created. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_line_id
foreignFields.description: Specific order line that consumes this reservation. {@link shopping_mall_order_lines.id}.

plainFields.name: reserved_quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units reserved for the related order line.

plainFields.name: reservation_state
plainFields.description: Current state of the reservation such as pending, active, consumed, expired, or cancelled.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reservation expires if payment is not completed. Null if managed by other business rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reservation record was created.

plainFields.name: consumed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reservation was consumed into a paid order or otherwise finalized.

plainFields.name: cancelled_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reservation was cancelled without consumption. Null when still active or consumed.

models.name: shopping_mall_inventory_movements
models.description:
Historical record of inventory quantity changes per SKU.

Each row captures a single business event that changes inventory quantities for an {@link shopping_mall_inventory_items} record, such as restock, manual adjustment, order capture, cancellation, or return.

Movements allow audit and reconciliation of stock levels over time. They can optionally reference order lines or reservations to tie stock changes to commercial events.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the inventory movement record.

foreignFields.name: inventory_item_id
foreignFields.description: Inventory item whose quantities were changed by this movement. {@link shopping_mall_inventory_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Optional order related to this movement, for example when stock is deducted for a sale. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_line_id
foreignFields.description: Optional order line related to this movement, giving more granular context. {@link shopping_mall_order_lines.id}.

foreignFields.name: reservation_id
foreignFields.description: Optional reservation that triggered this movement, used for transitions from reserved to sold or released. {@link shopping_mall_inventory_reservations.id}.

plainFields.name: movement_type
plainFields.description: Category of the movement such as restock, sale, cancellation_release, return_restock, return_nonrestock, manual_adjustment, or correction.

plainFields.name: quantity_delta
plainFields.description: Signed quantity change applied to on-hand stock, where positive values increase stock and negative values decrease stock.

plainFields.name: reserved_delta
plainFields.description: Signed change applied to reserved quantity, used when reservations are created or released.

plainFields.name: resulting_on_hand_quantity
plainFields.description: On-hand quantity for the inventory item immediately after this movement was applied.

plainFields.name: resulting_reserved_quantity
plainFields.description: Reserved quantity for the inventory item immediately after this movement was applied.

plainFields.name: resulting_available_to_sell_quantity
plainFields.description: Available-to-sell quantity for the inventory item immediately after this movement was applied.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable reason or note explaining why this movement occurred.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this movement record was created. Represents the time the inventory change was applied.

models.name: shopping_mall_fulfillments
models.description:
Per-order-line fulfillment aggregate representing physical processing state.

Each record corresponds to the fulfillment lifecycle of a single {@link shopping_mall_order_lines} entry. It tracks how far the seller has progressed, including packing, shipping, delivery, and failure or return states.

Fulfillments connect order lines to shipments via {@link shopping_mall_fulfillment_items}. They enable clear separation between financial order state and physical movement of goods.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the fulfillment record.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Order that owns the order line being fulfilled. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_line_id
foreignFields.description: Order line whose physical fulfillment is represented by this record. {@link shopping_mall_order_lines.id}.

plainFields.name: fulfillment_status
plainFields.description: Business-defined fulfillment status such as pending, pending_fulfillment, packed, ready_to_ship, shipped, delivered, delivery_failed, returned, or lost.

plainFields.name: packed_quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of the order line that has been packed and is ready or already assigned to shipments.

plainFields.name: shipped_quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of the order line that has been shipped across all shipments.

plainFields.name: delivered_quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of the order line that has been confirmed as delivered across all shipments.

plainFields.name: last_status_reason
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable explanation for the current fulfillment status, such as delivery failure reason or manual notes.

plainFields.name: packed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this fulfillment first reached a packed state.

plainFields.name: first_shipped_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when units in this fulfillment were first shipped.

plainFields.name: last_delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when units in this fulfillment were last marked as delivered.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this fulfillment record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this fulfillment record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this fulfillment record was soft-deleted. Null when active.

models.name: shopping_mall_fulfillment_items
models.description:
Junction records connecting fulfillments to shipments with quantities.

Each row describes how much of a specific fulfillment (per order line) is included in a given shipment. This enables partial shipments and multiple shipments for a single order line.

The table is subsidiary, serving as a many-to-many link with additional quantitative context between {@link shopping_mall_fulfillments} and {@link shopping_mall_shipments}.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the fulfillment item record.

foreignFields.name: fulfillment_id
foreignFields.description: Fulfillment entity whose quantity is being shipped. {@link shopping_mall_fulfillments.id}.

foreignFields.name: shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Shipment that carries part or all of the fulfillment quantity. {@link shopping_mall_shipments.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of the fulfillment’s order line included in this shipment.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this fulfillment item link was created.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipments
models.description:
Physical shipments grouping one or more fulfillment items.

Each shipment represents a package or logical shipping unit that can contain items from one or more fulfillments of a single seller segment. It tracks high-level status, carrier, and tracking reference used for customer-facing order tracking.

Shipments link back to {@link shopping_mall_order_seller_segments} to respect multi-seller orders and isolate seller responsibilities. Detailed tracking milestones are stored in {@link shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events}.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the shipment record.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Customer-facing order that this shipment belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_seller_segment_id
foreignFields.description: Seller segment within the order that this shipment serves. {@link shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.id}.

plainFields.name: shipment_status
plainFields.description: High-level shipment status such as pending, ready_to_ship, shipped, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, delivery_failed, or lost.

plainFields.name: carrier_name
plainFields.description: Name of the carrier handling this shipment, such as a logistics company or postal service.

plainFields.name: carrier_service_level
plainFields.description: Optional service level name from the carrier, for example standard, express, or next_day.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Primary tracking number assigned by the carrier for this shipment, used for both internal and customer-facing tracking links.

plainFields.name: shipped_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment was handed over to the carrier.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment was confirmed delivered by the carrier or seller.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was soft-deleted. Null while active.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events
models.description:
Detailed tracking events for shipments from carriers or internal systems.

Each record represents a point-in-time status update for a {@link shopping_mall_shipments} record, such as in_transit, arrived_at_hub, out_for_delivery, delivered, or delivery_failed. It may also record location and free-form carrier messages.

These events allow reconstruction of the shipment journey and are important for customer support and dispute resolution. They are append-only and typically not soft-deleted.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the shipment tracking event record.

foreignFields.name: shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Shipment whose tracking status is being updated. {@link shopping_mall_shipments.id}.

plainFields.name: carrier_status_code
plainFields.description: Optional status code as provided by the carrier, capturing vendor-specific status values.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Normalized shipment tracking status such as shipped, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, delivery_failed, or exception.

plainFields.name: location_description
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable description of the shipment location, such as city or facility name.

plainFields.name: carrier_raw_message
plainFields.description: Optional free-form message from the carrier describing this tracking event.

plainFields.name: occurred_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tracking event occurred according to carrier or internal records.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tracking event record was created in the system.

models.name: shopping_mall_backorder_settings
models.description:
Per-inventory-item configuration for backorders.

Defines whether backorders are allowed for a given {@link shopping_mall_inventory_items} record and, if so, within what quantitative limits. Backorders permit orders even when available-to-sell quantity is zero, relying on future stock replenishment.

The table is in a 1:1 relationship with inventory items for which backorders are explicitly configured. It is subsidiary because it only provides configuration for the primary inventory entity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the backorder settings record.

foreignFields.name: inventory_item_id
foreignFields.description: Inventory item that these backorder settings apply to. {@link shopping_mall_inventory_items.id}.

plainFields.name: allow_backorder
plainFields.description: Indicates whether backorders are allowed for this inventory item when available-to-sell is non-positive.

plainFields.name: max_backorder_quantity
plainFields.description: Maximum number of units that may be placed on backorder across all customers. Null means unlimited or governed by higher-level policies.

plainFields.name: backorder_message
plainFields.description: Optional customer-facing message used when the item is sold in backorder mode, such as extended delivery times.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this backorder settings record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this backorder settings record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this backorder settings record was soft-deleted. Null when active.

models.name: shopping_mall_preorder_settings
models.description:
Per-inventory-item configuration for preorders.

Defines preorder behavior for inventory items that may be sold before stock physically exists, for example product launches. Preorders enable customers to place orders ahead of availability and restrict quantities or time windows according to policy.

The table is in a 1:1 relationship with {@link shopping_mall_inventory_items} for which preorder rules are explicitly defined and is considered subsidiary configuration data.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the preorder settings record.

foreignFields.name: inventory_item_id
foreignFields.description: Inventory item that these preorder settings apply to. {@link shopping_mall_inventory_items.id}.

plainFields.name: allow_preorder
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this inventory item can be sold as a preorder before regular stock becomes available.

plainFields.name: preorder_start_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when preorder sales are allowed to start for this item. Null when controlled by other policies.

plainFields.name: preorder_end_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp after which preorder sales are no longer allowed. Null when open-ended or controlled elsewhere.

plainFields.name: max_preorder_quantity
plainFields.description: Maximum number of units that may be sold in preorder across all customers. Null means unlimited or governed by higher-level policies.

plainFields.name: release_date
plainFields.description: Expected release or availability date used for customer communication and fulfillment planning.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this preorder settings record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this preorder settings record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this preorder settings record was soft-deleted. Null when active.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_reviews
models.description:
Customer-authored product reviews and star ratings.

Stores individual reviews created by customers for products they have purchased. Each review contains a numeric rating, an optional textual comment, and state indicating whether it is visible in public listings.

The table links each review to a specific product and optionally to a concrete SKU variant when reviews are configured at SKU level. It also links to the customer who authored the review and supports standard temporal fields for audit and soft deletion.

Moderation state is stored here for fast filtering, while detailed moderation history is kept in {@link shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events}. Aggregated rating statistics per product are stored separately in {@link shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates}.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the product review record.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the product being reviewed. References the catalog product entity. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Optional identifier of the specific SKU variant being reviewed when SKU-level reviews are enabled. {@link shopping_mall_product_skus.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who authored the review. {@link shopping_mall_customer.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Star rating value provided by the customer. Uses a fixed integer scale such as 15 inclusive, where the lowest value indicates the worst experience and the highest value the best.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Optional short summary or headline for the review. Shown in listing views where a brief title is helpful.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Optional free-form text comment describing the customer experience, subject to length limits and content policies.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Moderation and lifecycle status of the review. Typical values include pending, approved, hidden, rejected, and removed, and determine public visibility and eligibility for aggregation.

plainFields.name: is_public
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the review is currently visible in public product review lists. Derived from status but stored for efficient filtering.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review record was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review record was last updated, including moderation changes or customer edits.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the review was soft-deleted. Null when the review is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_review_reports
models.description:
Reports and abuse flags submitted against product reviews.

Stores complaints created by customers, sellers, or administrators about specific product reviews. Each report records who reported the review, why they reported it, and when the report was created.

Reports feed moderation workflows and help surface reviews that may contain spam, abusive language, policy violations, or other issues. Detailed moderation decisions based on these reports are captured in {@link shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events}.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the review report record.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the review being reported. {@link shopping_mall_product_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: reporter_actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who submitted the report. Typical values include customer, seller, and platformAdmin and determine how reporter_actor_id is interpreted at the application level.

plainFields.name: reporter_actor_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the actor who submitted the report. Interpreted together with reporter_actor_type to reference customer, seller, or platform admin identities in their own tables.

plainFields.name: reason_code
plainFields.description: Structured reason code categorizing why the review was reported, such as spam, inappropriate_language, privacy_violation, off_topic, or conflict_of_interest.

plainFields.name: comment
plainFields.description: Optional free-form comment from the reporter providing additional context or explanation for the report.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report record was last updated, for example when changing reason_code or comment.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the report was soft-deleted or logically cleared. Null while the report is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events
models.description:
Historical moderation actions applied to product reviews.

Captures an append-only timeline of moderation decisions taken for each review, such as approving, hiding, rejecting, or removing content. Each event links to the target review and the platform administrator who performed the action.

This table provides an immutable audit trail for compliance and dispute resolution, complementing the current status fields stored on {@link shopping_mall_product_reviews}. It supports queries over moderation history by review, by admin actor, or by event type.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the moderation event record.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the review to which this moderation decision applies. {@link shopping_mall_product_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: platformadmin_id
foreignFields.description: Platform administrator who performed the moderation action. {@link shopping_mall_platformadmin.id}.

plainFields.name: from_status
plainFields.description: Previous moderation status of the review before this event was applied. Null for the initial moderation event when there is no prior status.

plainFields.name: to_status
plainFields.description: New moderation status of the review after this event, such as approved, hidden, rejected, or removed.

plainFields.name: reason_code
plainFields.description: Optional structured reason code describing why this moderation action was taken, for example policy_violation, abuse, spam, or legal_request.

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description: Optional free-form note provided by the moderator with additional context or justification for the decision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation event was recorded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation event record was last updated, usually matching created_at in append-only usage.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the moderation event was logically removed from active views. Null under normal append-only usage.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses
models.description:
Seller-authored responses to customer product reviews.

Stores optional replies written by sellers in response to customer reviews of their products. Each response is associated with exactly one review and one seller and is constrained so that at most one response exists per review.

Seller responses allow merchants to address feedback publicly while keeping the original review content unchanged. Visibility and moderation of responses can be coordinated with the parent review and overall moderation policies.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the seller response record.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the review this seller response is attached to. Enforced as 1:1 so each review has at most one response. {@link shopping_mall_product_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who authored the response. {@link shopping_mall_seller.id}.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Text content of the seller response visible to customers, subject to moderation and content policies.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller response was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller response was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the seller response was soft-deleted or hidden from public view.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates
models.description:
Materialized aggregate ratings and review counts per product and optional SKU.

Caches denormalized statistics derived from {@link shopping_mall_product_reviews}, such as average rating and total count of contributing reviews. This table is optimized for fast catalog and product-detail queries that require rating summaries without scanning all individual reviews.

Entries are typically maintained by background jobs or transactional update logic whenever reviews are created, edited, or re-moderated. It supports both product-level and SKU-level aggregates when SKU-specific reviews are enabled.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the rating aggregate record.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the product for which rating aggregates are computed. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Optional identifier of the SKU variant when aggregates are calculated at SKU level. Null for product-level aggregates. {@link shopping_mall_product_skus.id}.

plainFields.name: average_rating
plainFields.description: Average rating value for this product or SKU based on approved reviews. Null when no contributing reviews exist.

plainFields.name: review_count
plainFields.description: Total number of reviews contributing to this aggregate for the product or SKU, typically counting only approved and public reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_1_count
plainFields.description: Number of contributing reviews with the lowest rating value (for example, 1 star) for this product or SKU.

plainFields.name: rating_2_count
plainFields.description: Number of contributing reviews with rating value 2 for this product or SKU when using a 15 scale.

plainFields.name: rating_3_count
plainFields.description: Number of contributing reviews with rating value 3 for this product or SKU when using a 15 scale.

plainFields.name: rating_4_count
plainFields.description: Number of contributing reviews with rating value 4 for this product or SKU when using a 15 scale.

plainFields.name: rating_5_count
plainFields.description: Number of contributing reviews with the highest rating value (for example, 5 stars) for this product or SKU.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the aggregate record was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the aggregate record was last recalculated or updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp indicating when this aggregate was logically removed, for example when the product is deprecated. Null while active.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_action_audits
models.description:
Audit records for administrative actions performed by platform administrators.

Each row represents a single state-changing or sensitive read operation triggered by a platformAdmin across any domain (users, sellers, products, orders, payments, reviews, configuration, etc.).

The model links to the acting {@link shopping_mall_platformadmin} and captures generic target information via target_type and target_id fields, so it can represent actions on many different entity types without polymorphic foreign keys.

These records are append-only and are used for compliance audits, forensic investigations, and internal reporting about admin behavior.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the admin action audit record.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_platformadmin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the platform administrator who performed the action. {@link shopping_mall_platformadmin.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: High-level category of the admin action (for example, user_status_change, product_visibility_update, refund_approval, seller_suspension).

plainFields.name: action_subtype
plainFields.description: Optional more granular subtype or reason code for the action, used to distinguish specific flows within the action_type.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Business type of the primary target resource of this action (for example, customer, seller, product, order, payment, review, configuration).

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: Opaque identifier string of the primary target resource. Stores the ID value from the target table as text to avoid polymorphic foreign keys.

plainFields.name: secondary_target_type
plainFields.description: Optional business type of a secondary target resource affected by the action, when applicable.

plainFields.name: secondary_target_id
plainFields.description: Optional opaque identifier string of a secondary target resource affected by the action.

plainFields.name: request_context
plainFields.description: Optional serialized context about the request, such as IP address, user agent, or admin dashboard module information, stored as text or JSON string.

plainFields.name: before_snapshot
plainFields.description: Optional snapshot of key fields from before the action, stored as a serialized JSON string for audit comparison.

plainFields.name: after_snapshot
plainFields.description: Optional snapshot of key fields from after the action, stored as a serialized JSON string for audit comparison.

plainFields.name: action_summary
plainFields.description: Human-readable summary of the action, suitable for audit UI and reports.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this admin action was recorded.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs
models.description:
Audit log of configuration changes made by platform administrators.

Each record represents a single logical change to platform-wide configuration or policy settings, such as cancellation windows, refund policies, review rules, or risk thresholds.

The log links to the acting {@link shopping_mall_platformadmin} and stores generic information about which configuration domain was changed, what keys were affected, and serialized before/after values. This table is append-only and used for compliance and debugging of configuration-related behavior.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the configuration change log record.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_platformadmin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the platform administrator who changed the configuration. {@link shopping_mall_platformadmin.id}.

plainFields.name: config_domain
plainFields.description: Logical domain of the configuration that was changed (for example, cancellation_policy, refund_policy, review_policy, inventory_settings, risk_settings).

plainFields.name: config_scope
plainFields.description: Optional scope information for the configuration change (for example, region code, category, or specific seller scope).

plainFields.name: changed_keys_summary
plainFields.description: Short textual summary of which configuration keys or sections were modified, used for quick scanning and search.

plainFields.name: before_value
plainFields.description: Serialized representation of the configuration values before the change, typically stored as a JSON string.

plainFields.name: after_value
plainFields.description: Serialized representation of the configuration values after the change, typically stored as a JSON string.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable justification or comment entered by the admin explaining why the configuration was changed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration change was recorded.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries
models.description:
Periodic performance summaries and risk indicators for individual sellers.

Each row aggregates metrics for a specific {@link shopping_mall_seller} over a defined time period (for example, daily, weekly, or monthly). Metrics can include order volume, cancellation rates, refund rates, dispute counts, review distributions, and other KPIs.

These records are used by platformAdmin to monitor seller health, identify risk patterns, and feed rule-based or manual interventions. They are append-only snapshots rather than live counters.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the seller performance summary record.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the seller whose performance is summarized. {@link shopping_mall_seller.id}.

plainFields.name: period_start
plainFields.description: Start timestamp of the period this summary covers (inclusive).

plainFields.name: period_end
plainFields.description: End timestamp of the period this summary covers (exclusive or inclusive, according to reporting conventions).

plainFields.name: orders_count
plainFields.description: Total count of orders that contained this seller’s items during the period.

plainFields.name: cancelled_orders_count
plainFields.description: Count of orders or order segments cancelled for this seller during the period.

plainFields.name: refunded_orders_count
plainFields.description: Count of orders or order segments for this seller that had refunds processed during the period.

plainFields.name: dispute_opened_count
plainFields.description: Number of disputes opened against this seller’s orders during the period.

plainFields.name: dispute_resolved_against_seller_count
plainFields.description: Number of disputes resolved against the seller (favoring the customer) during the period.

plainFields.name: average_rating
plainFields.description: Average product review rating for this seller’s products during the period, based on contributing reviews. Nullable if no reviews exist.

plainFields.name: low_rating_review_count
plainFields.description: Count of low-rated reviews (for example, 1–2 stars) for this seller’s products during the period.

plainFields.name: risk_level
plainFields.description: Categorical risk level derived from metrics (for example, low, medium, high, critical).

plainFields.name: risk_reason_summary
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable summary explaining why the seller was assigned the given risk_level for this period.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this performance summary snapshot was generated.

models.name: shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs
models.description:
Resolution history for order disputes handled by sellers, platform administrators, or automated systems.

Each record represents a discrete resolution decision or state change for a particular {@link shopping_mall_order_disputes} instance. It captures who made the decision (seller or platform admin through foreign keys, or an automated system via actor_type), what outcome was chosen, and the rationale.

The actor_type field describes the logical actor category (for example, seller, platform_admin, automated_rule). When actor_type is seller, the shopping_mall_seller_id field MUST be populated. When actor_type is platform_admin, the shopping_mall_platformadmin_id field MUST be populated. For automated or system-driven resolutions, both foreign keys may be null.

These logs provide a complete audit trail for dispute handling and support compliance reviews, conflict-of-interest checks, and quality monitoring of dispute resolutions. Indexes are optimized for querying timelines per dispute, filtering by outcome, and looking up records by the concrete human actor when present.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the dispute resolution log record.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_dispute_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the order dispute to which this resolution event belongs. {@link shopping_mall_order_disputes.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_platformadmin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the platform administrator who made or approved this resolution decision, when the actor_type is platform_admin. {@link shopping_mall_platformadmin.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the seller who made this resolution decision when the actor_type is seller. {@link shopping_mall_seller.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor that performed this resolution action (for example, seller, platform_admin, automated_rule). Determines which concrete actor foreign key must be present when the actor is a human.

plainFields.name: resolution_outcome
plainFields.description: Outcome code of the resolution step (for example, refund_approved_full, refund_approved_partial, refund_rejected, replacement_issued, goodwill_credit).

plainFields.name: resolution_rationale
plainFields.description: Detailed human-readable explanation of why this resolution outcome was chosen.

plainFields.name: notes_internal
plainFields.description: Optional internal notes for platform use only, not exposed to customers or sellers.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this resolution event was recorded.

models.name: shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions
models.description:
Definitions of fraud and risk rules evaluated against orders, payments, accounts, or other events.

Each record describes a single business rule that can detect suspicious behavior or policy violations. Rules are configured and maintained by platformAdmin and may be evaluated by background services or at runtime.

The table stores metadata such as rule code, severity, scope, and a serialized rule_expression that external engines can interpret. It also tracks enabled state and lifecycle timestamps.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the fraud or risk rule definition.

foreignFields.name: created_by_platformadmin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the platform administrator who originally created this rule definition. {@link shopping_mall_platformadmin.id}.

foreignFields.name: updated_by_platformadmin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the platform administrator who last updated this rule definition. {@link shopping_mall_platformadmin.id}.

plainFields.name: rule_code
plainFields.description: Stable business identifier for the rule, unique across all fraud_rule_definitions (for example, HIGH_REFUND_RATE, MULTIPLE_CARDS_SAME_IP).

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable name for this rule, used in admin tools and reports.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the rule’s purpose, detection logic, and expected handling guidance for admins.

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Configured severity level of this rule (for example, low, medium, high, critical) used for prioritization and alerting.

plainFields.name: scope
plainFields.description: Scope of entities the rule applies to (for example, order, payment, customer_account, seller_account, session_activity).

plainFields.name: rule_expression
plainFields.description: Machine-interpretable expression or configuration payload that encodes the rule logic, stored as a JSON or DSL string. The evaluation engine interprets this expression.

plainFields.name: is_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether this rule is currently active and should be evaluated by the fraud engine.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this rule definition was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this rule definition was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp when this rule was logically removed from use. Null when the rule is still part of history or active configuration.

models.name: shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations
models.description:
Recorded violations or hits of configured fraud and risk rules.

Each row represents a single evaluation event where a {@link shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions} rule triggered for a particular actor or transaction. It captures the rule, the entity context (actor_type and actor_id), associated order if any, and descriptive information about why the rule fired.

These records are used for risk analysis dashboards, manual review queues, escalation workflows, and to correlate fraud patterns across customers, sellers, orders, and payment instruments.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the fraud rule violation record.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definition_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the fraud rule definition that was violated. {@link shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the related order when the violation concerns a specific order. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor or entity the violation is associated with (for example, customer, seller, platform_admin, session, payment_method).

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: Opaque identifier string of the actor or entity the violation is associated with, stored as text to support multiple target types.

plainFields.name: violation_severity
plainFields.description: Severity classification of this particular violation instance (for example, info, warning, critical), which may match or refine the rule’s severity.

plainFields.name: violation_reason
plainFields.description: Detailed human-readable explanation of why this rule fired, often including key metric values or threshold comparisons.

plainFields.name: evaluation_context
plainFields.description: Serialized evaluation payload or context used when the rule was evaluated, stored as JSON or another structured format for later inspection.

plainFields.name: occurred_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the rule evaluation that produced this violation occurred.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this violation record was stored.

models.name: shopping_mall_auth_logs
models.description:
Authentication-related log entries for login, logout, and token lifecycle events.

Captures security-relevant information about authentication attempts and session lifecycle for all actor types (customer, seller, platformAdmin) as well as guest-to-customer transitions. Each row represents an immutable point-in-time event, such as a successful login, failed login, token refresh, or logout.

The table intentionally stores denormalized identifiers (such as email and actor_role) as observed at the time of the event. Core identity and session tables from other components may reference these log entries when performing investigations, but this model does not maintain foreign keys to them to keep the Logs component decoupled.

Operations and security teams use these logs for incident response, fraud detection support, and compliance reporting around authentication behavior.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for this authentication log entry.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: High-level type of authentication event. Examples include "login_success", "login_failure", "logout", "token_refresh", "password_reset_request", and "password_reset_success".

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Logical actor type associated with the event, if known. Typical values are "guestUser", "customer", "seller", or "platformAdmin". Null when the actor type cannot be determined (for example, malformed requests).

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: Opaque identifier of the actor record at the time of the event, when available. This can refer to a customer, seller, or platform admin record depending on actor_type. Stored as raw UUID without a foreign key to keep this component independent.

plainFields.name: actor_email
plainFields.description: Email address presented or associated with the authentication event. Captured as plain text to allow investigation of repeated failed attempts. May be null for token-only flows or where email is not used.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the authentication event originated. Useful for security analysis and anomaly detection. May be IPv4 or IPv6 formatted string.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Raw user agent string supplied by the client, if available. Used for device and browser fingerprinting during security investigations.

plainFields.name: success
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the authentication event is considered successful from the business perspective. For example, true for completed logins and successful token refreshes, false for failed login attempts.

plainFields.name: failure_reason
plainFields.description: Business-level reason for authentication failure, when success is false. Examples include "invalid_credentials", "account_suspended", "password_expired", or "rate_limited". Null for successful events.

plainFields.name: session_id
plainFields.description: Opaque identifier referencing a session record in its own domain, when a session is involved. Stored as UUID without explicit foreign key to avoid cross-component coupling.

plainFields.name: correlation_id
plainFields.description: Correlation identifier that ties this authentication event to a broader request or workflow. Used to trace multi-step interactions across logs.

plainFields.name: metadata_json
plainFields.description: Optional JSON-encoded string carrying additional structured metadata about the event, such as region, risk scores, or MFA method. The schema is intentionally flexible and interpreted by application logic.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this authentication event was recorded. Represents the effective time of the event for analysis purposes.

models.name: shopping_mall_access_logs
models.description:
High-level access log entries for API or web requests handled by the platform.

Each row describes a single logical request as seen by the backend, including metadata such as HTTP method, path, status code, latency, actor context, and client information. These logs are primarily used for observability, performance monitoring, and security analytics.

The model stores denormalized copies of actor identity attributes and request metadata without foreign keys to core domain tables. This allows the Logs component to remain independent while still supporting rich analysis of traffic and behavior patterns across customers, sellers, and admins.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for this access log entry.

plainFields.name: request_id
plainFields.description: Application-level identifier for the request, if one was generated. Used to correlate this access log with other technical logs or traces.

plainFields.name: correlation_id
plainFields.description: Correlation identifier linking this request to a broader workflow or user interaction that may span multiple services or events.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Logical actor type that executed the request when known, such as "guestUser", "customer", "seller", or "platformAdmin". Null when no actor context is associated with the request.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: Opaque identifier of the actor that performed the request, when available. This might correspond to a customer, seller, or admin in the core domain, but no foreign key is enforced here.

plainFields.name: actor_role
plainFields.description: Role or permission profile applied during authorization evaluation for this request. This can be more specific than actor_type, such as an admin role name.

plainFields.name: http_method
plainFields.description: HTTP method of the request as seen by the backend, such as "GET", "POST", "PUT", or "DELETE".

plainFields.name: path
plainFields.description: Normalized request path or route template for the accessed endpoint. Used for grouping and analyzing traffic per API surface.

plainFields.name: query_string
plainFields.description: Raw query string or a normalized representation of query parameters, if captured. Useful for debugging and analytics. May be null if not recorded.

plainFields.name: status_code
plainFields.description: HTTP status code returned to the client for this request, such as 200, 400, or 500.

plainFields.name: success
plainFields.description: Boolean indicator that the business operation completed successfully from the platform perspective. Typically true for 2xx responses, false for 4xx and 5xx, but can be customized by application logic.

plainFields.name: latency_ms
plainFields.description: Total time in milliseconds spent processing this request on the backend, excluding client network latency. Used for performance monitoring and SLO tracking.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address from which the request originated. May be derived from headers such as X-Forwarded-For in proxy setups.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Raw user agent string associated with the request. Provides insight into client device and browser characteristics.

plainFields.name: referer
plainFields.description: HTTP Referer header value when present, indicating the previous page or origin of the request. Useful for traffic flow analysis.

plainFields.name: request_body_truncated
plainFields.description: Optional truncated representation of the request body, redacted to avoid sensitive information. Intended for debugging problematic calls and is stored as a plain string or JSON snippet.

plainFields.name: response_body_truncated
plainFields.description: Optional truncated representation of the response body, redacted to avoid sensitive information. Useful for troubleshooting and verifying business behavior.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this access log entry was recorded. Typically corresponds to the time when the response was sent to the client.

models.name: shopping_mall_error_logs
models.description:
Application error and exception logs capturing failures in business flows and technical operations.

Each row represents a single error event, such as an unhandled exception, failed business rule evaluation, or external dependency failure that surfaces as an error in the backend. These logs are essential for incident analysis, debugging, and reliability improvements.

The model includes context fields like error_code, severity, message, stack summary, and a generic context JSON payload. It also records correlation and request identifiers to allow cross-referencing with access and integration logs. No foreign keys are used so that the Logs component remains independent of specific domain schemas.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for this error log entry.

plainFields.name: error_code
plainFields.description: Application-specific error code or symbolic identifier for this error condition. Examples include domain-specific codes such as "ORDER_VALIDATION_FAILED" or "PAYMENT_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT".

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Severity level of the error as determined by the application, such as "info", "warning", "error", or "critical". Used to prioritize incident response.

plainFields.name: message
plainFields.description: Human-readable error message summarizing the failure. May be redacted to avoid exposing sensitive information while still helping debugging.

plainFields.name: stack_trace
plainFields.description: Captured stack trace or stack summary for the error, if available. May be truncated or sanitized to control volume and protect sensitive data.

plainFields.name: context_json
plainFields.description: JSON-encoded string containing structured context about the error, such as input identifiers, business parameters, or state snapshots. The schema is flexible and controlled by application code.

plainFields.name: request_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the request during which the error occurred, when known. Used for correlating with access logs and higher-level traces.

plainFields.name: correlation_id
plainFields.description: Correlation identifier tying this error to a broader workflow, saga, or asynchronous process across services.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Logical actor type affected by the error, such as "guestUser", "customer", "seller", or "platformAdmin". May be null for purely background or system-level errors.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: Opaque identifier of the actor related to this error, when applicable. Stored as UUID without enforcing foreign key constraints.

plainFields.name: service_name
plainFields.description: Logical name of the service or bounded context that produced the error. Useful in multi-service or modular architectures.

plainFields.name: component_name
plainFields.description: Name of the component, module, or subsystem within the service where the error originated, such as a domain area or technical layer.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this error event was recorded. Represents the time at which the failure was observed by the backend.

models.name: shopping_mall_integration_event_logs
models.description:
Logs for interactions with external integration partners and infrastructure services.

Each row captures a single outbound or inbound integration event involving external payment providers, email services, shipping carriers, fraud engines, or other third-party systems. Events include requests, callbacks, notifications, and asynchronous messages.

The model records provider type, provider name, event type, direction (outbound or inbound), technical and business statuses, timing information, and optional payload snippets. Correlation and request IDs allow cross-referencing with other logs. No foreign keys are maintained so that logs remain independent and can be written even when core transactional operations fail.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for this integration event log entry.

plainFields.name: provider_type
plainFields.description: High-level category of external provider involved in the integration event, such as "payment", "email", "shipping", "fraud", or "analytics".

plainFields.name: provider_name
plainFields.description: Specific provider name or identifier, such as a payment gateway or carrier code. Used for per-provider reliability and SLA analysis.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Business-level type of integration event, such as "authorization_request", "capture", "refund", "tracking_update", or "webhook_notification".

plainFields.name: direction
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the event is outbound from shoppingMall to the provider (for example, API call) or inbound from the provider to shoppingMall (for example, webhook). Typical values include "outbound" and "inbound".

plainFields.name: request_id
plainFields.description: Identifier associated with the request within the platform, when the integration call is part of a larger flow. Enables correlation with access and error logs.

plainFields.name: provider_request_id
plainFields.description: Identifier assigned by the external provider to the request or message, if available. Useful for provider-side support and reconciliation.

plainFields.name: provider_response_id
plainFields.description: Identifier for the provider response or transaction, when distinct from provider_request_id. Often used in payment and shipping APIs.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Overall status of the integration event from the platform perspective, such as "success", "failure", or "timeout".

plainFields.name: http_status_code
plainFields.description: HTTP status code returned by the provider for outbound calls, where applicable. Null for non-HTTP integrations or inbound-only events without a direct code.

plainFields.name: latency_ms
plainFields.description: Elapsed time in milliseconds between sending a request and receiving a response from the external provider, for outbound events. May be null for inbound-only notifications or where not measured.

plainFields.name: error_code
plainFields.description: Provider-specific or platform-specific error code when status indicates failure. Facilitates troubleshooting and mapping of recurring integration issues.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Human-readable error message or description associated with a failed integration event, often derived from the provider response or internal handling.

plainFields.name: request_payload_truncated
plainFields.description: Optional truncated and sanitized representation of the request payload sent to the provider. Captured as a string or JSON snippet for debugging while avoiding sensitive content where required.

plainFields.name: response_payload_truncated
plainFields.description: Optional truncated and sanitized representation of the provider response payload. Used for debugging integration behavior without storing full raw messages.

plainFields.name: correlation_id
plainFields.description: Correlation identifier that links this integration event to other application-level operations, such as orders or payments, across different log tables.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this integration event log entry was recorded. Represents the time the platform processed the event.
